findings.title: queued timestamp is evaluated once at import time
findings.body: The `queued` field defaults to `timezone.now()` at class definition time, so every `AssignmentSource` constructed without an explicit `queued` value shares the same module-import timestamp. If `queued` is meant to represent when each assignment source was queued, it will be wrong for all instances. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` or set it in `__post_init__` if a dynamic timestamp is intended.

findings.title: Malformed assignment source disables cycle guard
findings.body: `from_dict` swallows `ValueError` and `TypeError` and returns `None`. In `sync_assignee_outbound`, a non-empty malformed `assignment_source_dict` therefore becomes `None`, and `should_sync` cannot compare integration IDs, so the outbound sync to the originating integration is allowed. The guard should fail closed or retry if an assignment source was supplied but cannot be parsed; otherwise the sync loop this PR fixes can reappear if serialization or schema issues produce an invalid dict.

findings.title: No coverage that non-matching source integrations still sync
findings.body: The new `should_sync` guard is only tested for the matching source integration (`assert_not_called`) and for `assignment_source=None`. The comment in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync` says other integrations should still propagate changes outward, but there is no test with an assignment source from integration A and an external issue linked to integration B asserting that `sync_assignee_outbound` is called. An overbroad comparison would pass the current tests and silently stop cross-integration sync.
